What Staying with Zapmed Means for Your Care Going Forward

Change can be disorienting, especially when it involves something as personal as your healthcare.

One thing worth knowing is that once you are registered and have had your first consultation, you are fully set up within the Zapmed system. Your doctor will have your current health information on file, your consultations will be logged, and your ongoing care will be managed in one place.

We also remain committed to removing the barriers that so often make healthcare feel inaccessible, from long waiting times to the inconvenience of in-person visits for matters that can be handled remotely. That commitment shapes every part of how Zapmed is built and how it continues to grow.

We’re glad you’re here, and we look forward to being a consistent, trusted presence in your health for the years ahead.

posts.title: How to Access Your Zapmed Invoice to Claim from Your Medical Aid
posts.excerpt: Living in South Africa, we all know that the true value of a medical aid lies in its ability to cushion the blow of healthcare costs.
posts.body:
Living in South Africa, we all know that the true value of a medical aid lies in its ability to cushion the blow of healthcare costs. 

Whether you are on a long-term prescription for birth control or seeking once-off treatment for a sexually transmitted infection, having that financial safety net makes a world of difference. When you choose modern telehealth, you are opting for convenience, but you still want to ensure your monthly contributions work for you. 

Understanding the intersection of digital scripts and scheme reimbursements is the best way to keep your wellness journey affordable while enjoying the privacy and ease of home delivery.

Today, we are diving into a real patient question that landed in our inbox:

How do I obtain my invoice to claim from my medical aid?

This guide walks you through exactly how that works, what local schemes cover, and the specific details you need to submit a successful claim.

How Do I Obtain My Zapmed Invoice to Claim from My Medical Aid?

After your Zapmed consultation, an invoice is sent directly to your email address. If you cannot find it in your inbox, check your spam folder first. You can also log into your Zapmed patient portal and download the invoice from there at any time.

Your invoice will include all the details your medical aid needs to process a claim: the consultation date, the service rendered, and the relevant billing codes. Keep this document saved somewhere accessible because you will need it when submitting your claim online or at your scheme’s branch.

Table of Contents

  • How Do I Obtain My Zapmed Invoice to Claim from My Medical Aid?
  • Which Medical Aids Typically Reimburse Zapmed Costs?
  • Step-by-Step: How to Claim Your Zapmed Consultation Fee from Medical Aid
  • What Your Medical Aid Covers vs. Cash Costs
  • The Backup Plan
  • Savings vs. Day-to-Day Benefits: Where Does Your Zapmed Claim Go?

Which Medical Aids Typically Reimburse Zapmed Costs?

South Africa’s major schemes generally support telehealth consultations, but reimbursement rates and processes differ.

Discovery Health reimburses consultations from your Medical Savings Account (MSA) or Personal Health Fund, depending on your plan. Discovery uses the Discovery Health Rate (DHR); if Zapmed’s fee exceeds this, a co-payment may apply. Claims should be submitted via the Discovery Health app. For medication, claims are processed by the dispensing pharmacy, though members on KeyCare or Smart plans must use network-specific pharmacies to avoid out-of-pocket costs.

Bonitas processes claims for consultations through your day-to-day benefits or savings. To claim, you must submit a valid Zapmed tax invoice (including a practice number and ICD-10 code) via the Bonitas member app or web portal. Prescription claims are subject to the Bonitas Pharmacy Network; using a non-network pharmacy may trigger a 20% to 30% co-payment.

Momentum Medical Scheme and Fedhealth both recognise telehealth. Momentum members typically fund these via their HealthSaver or MSA, with a standard virtual consultation rate often applied. Fedhealth members on flexiFED plans can use their Day-to-Day Plus (D2D+) benefit once unlocked via a Health Risk Assessment. Claims for both are managed through their respective apps using your digital invoice.

Medihelp and GEMS support day-to-day claims for GP-level consultations. GEMS members should be cautious of Designated Service Provider (DSP) restrictions; on options like Tanzanite One, using a non-network telehealth provider may lead to significant co-payments.

Across all schemes, always confirm your specific plan’s 2026 rules regarding “Virtual Care” benefits before assuming full reimbursement.

The Specifics Your Provider Needs

  • To ensure your claim is processed without being sent back for more information, your invoice includes three vital pieces of information.
  • Practice Number: This identifies the medical professional who treated you.
  • ICD-10 Codes: These are international codes that tell the medical aid what condition was treated.
  • Detailed Line Items: A breakdown of the service rendered.

When you submit these details via your medical aid’s member portal or app, the processing time usually takes a few business days.

Step-by-Step: How to Claim Your Zapmed Consultation Fee from Medical Aid

Step 1: Complete your Zapmed consultation

After your consultation, check your email for your invoice. If it has not arrived within a few hours, log in to your Zapmed patient portal and download it directly.

Step 2: Check your invoice details

Your invoice should reflect the consultation date, the service provided, and the relevant ICD-10 codes linked to your condition. ICD-10 codes are standardised diagnosis codes that medical aids require to process claims. If anything looks unclear, contact the Zapmed support team before submitting.

Step 3: Note the practice number

Zapmed’s practice number will appear on your invoice. Medical aid portals typically require this when submitting a claim for a consultation. Do not skip this field when filling in your claim form.

Step 4: Log in to your medical aid portal or app

Most major schemes now have online claim submission available. Discovery uses the Discovery Health app, Bonitas has its member portal, and Momentum uses the Multiply and Health app. Look for a section labelled “Submit a Claim” or “Day-to-Day Claims.”

Step 5: Upload your invoice

Attach your Zapmed invoice as your supporting document. Fill in the required fields: your membership number, the date of service, the practice number, and the ICD-10 code if prompted.

Step 6: Submit and track your claim

Once submitted, most schemes process claims within a few business days. You can track the status through the same portal. Reimbursements are paid directly into your registered bank account.

Step 7: For medication claims, let the pharmacy handle it

You do not need to submit a separate medication claim. Zapmed’s partner pharmacy does this automatically each month. If the claim is successful, great. If it is rejected, you will hear from Zapmed directly.

Please Like and Follow Our Facebook Page

What Your Medical Aid Covers vs. Cash Costs

Understanding exactly what gets billed where will save you a lot of back-and-forth with your scheme.

Service and consultation fees

Zapmed charges a consultation fee when you access care — R220 per month for subscription services, or R450 for a once-off consultation. These fees are paid upfront by you at the time of booking. Your medical aid does not settle these directly with Zapmed. However, you can submit your invoice to your medical aid provider and claim this amount back yourself, depending on your plan and available benefits.

Medication costs

This is where your medical aid does most of the work. Zapmed’s partner pharmacy submits your medication claim directly to your scheme each month, so you do not have to chase this yourself. If your medical aid covers the prescribed medication, it will be billed through your scheme. You simply choose at sign-up (on your personal details form) whether you want to pay for medication through medical aid or privately, and you can update that preference at any time. These changes will take effect from your next repeat.

Co-payments

Even when your medical aid does cover a medication, you may still pay a small portion out of pocket. This happens when your scheme does not cover the full cost of a specific brand, or when the prescribed product sits outside your plan’s approved medicine list (formulary). A generic alternative may be fully covered where a branded version is not. Your pharmacist or scheme can clarify this for the specific medication you have been prescribed.

The Backup Plan

Medical aid claims aren’t always a sure thing. A claim might be rejected if your savings are depleted for the year or if the scheme doesn’t recognise a specific treatment under your current plan. If this happens, don’t worry. We will get in touch to see if you would like to switch over to being a cash customer for that month. This ensures your treatment remains uninterrupted while you sort out the details with your provider.

Savings vs. Day-to-Day Benefits: Where Does Your Zapmed Claim Go?

Most Zapmed claims are processed against your Medical Savings Account (MSA) or your day-to-day benefit allocation, rather than your hospital or chronic disease benefit. This is important to understand before you assume a claim will be fully covered.

Your MSA is the portion of your monthly contribution set aside for everyday healthcare costs: GP visits, dentist trips, optometry, and general prescriptions. Telehealth consultations typically fall into this category. 

Once your MSA is depleted for the year, you either fall into a gap period (depending on your plan) or you begin paying from your own pocket until your new benefit year starts.

Some plans on Discovery, Bonitas, Momentum, and Fedhealth do allow day-to-day claims to be submitted for telehealth services, but the outcome depends on your specific plan option and benefit utilisation for the year. 

Chronic medication for conditions like hormonal contraception or hair loss treatments may qualify for your chronic benefit if your doctor has registered the condition under the appropriate ICD-10 code. Speak to your scheme directly to confirm what your specific plan allows.

  • READ NEXT: How to Prepare for Your First Online Doctor Consultation in South Africa

Wrapping Up

Telehealth is reshaping how South Africans access quality healthcare, and your medical aid can be part of that picture. You have already taken the first step by asking the right questions.If you have any questions about your invoice, your prescription, or what Zapmed can help you with, book a consultation, and our partner doctor will walk you through it.

posts.title: Where Are My Meds? A Simple Guide to Zapmed Delivery Tracking
posts.excerpt: When you hand over something as precious as your health to a telehealth service, you're placing a lot of trust in that service. That's not something we take lightly at Zapmed.
posts.body:
[et_pb_section][et_pb_row][et_pb_column type=”4_4″][et_pb_text]

When you hand over something as precious as your health to a telehealth service, you’re placing a lot of trust in that service. That’s not something we take lightly at Zapmed. Which is why we want every part of your experience, from consult to delivery, to feel effortless.

You chose Zapmed because you needed convenience—a quick online consult, a discreet prescription, and your medication delivered straight to your door. You don’t have time to wait around wondering when the courier will finally ring the bell.

We get it. When you’re waiting for healthcare products, time feels a little slower. You want to know exactly when your package will arrive so you can get on with your day. Recently, one of our community members reached out to us with a very common scenario:

“I believe my order should’ve been delivered yesterday or this morning. I cannot find the waybill to track it and only have an order number.”

If you’ve ever found yourself thinking, “Eish, I need to track my order Zapmed style, but I’ve lost the link,” or you’re simply wondering what the standard Zapmed delivery time is, you are in exactly the right place. Grab a cup of rooibos, take a breath, and let’s walk through exactly how our tracking process works, what to expect, and who to shout to if things go wrong.

How to track your Zapmed order (and what to do if it’s late)

Tracking your medication shouldn’t require a detective’s licence. We’ve designed the Zapmed delivery tracking system to be as transparent and user-friendly as possible, because the last thing you need is more admin. 

Let’s break down exactly how you can keep an eye on your parcel, what delivery times you can realistically expect based on where you live, and what steps to take if the courier seems to be playing hide-and-seek.

1. Understanding the Standard Zapmed Delivery Time

Before you start worrying that your package is lost in the courier ether, it’s helpful to know our standard delivery windows. South Africa is a big place, and while we work with top-tier courier partners to get your medication to you fast, turnaround times do depend on your province.

Here is what you can generally expect when you place an order with us:

  • Johannesburg and Surrounds (Same-Day Delivery): If you are based in Jozi and your prescription is finalised and paid for before our daily cut-off time (usually mid-morning), we hustle to get it to you on the very same day. We know city life moves fast, and we try to keep up.
  • Cape Town and Major Centres (Next-Day Delivery): For our patients in the Mother City, Durban, and Pretoria, you can usually expect your parcel the next working day.
  • Outlying and Regional Areas (48 Hours): If you live outside the major metropolitan hubs, say, in the beautiful Winelands, up the West Coast, or out in Mpumalanga, delivery usually takes around 48 hours. Our couriers need just a little extra time to reach you safely.

Note: Keep in mind that these timeframes apply to working days. If you finalise an order late on a Friday afternoon, the courier will only collect it on Monday morning.

2. Step-by-Step: Zapmed Delivery Tracking

So, your doctor has prescribed your medication, your payment has cleared, and your package is packed. Now what? Here is how you track it from our pharmacy to your front door.

Step 1: Check Your Messages for the Dispatch SMS

As soon as our courier partner scans your package at our facility, an automated SMS is triggered and sent straight to the email address you used during checkout.

Pro tip: If you don’t see it within 24 hours of your consultation, quickly check your spam or promotions folder. Sometimes our emails like to hide in there!

Step 2: Locate your Waybill Number and Tracking Link

Open your dispatch SMS. You will see a unique alphanumeric code. This is your Waybill Number. Below it, there will be a bright, clickable button that says “Track My Order”.

Step 3: Follow the Courier’s Live Updates

When you click the link, you will be taken directly to our courier partner’s tracking portal. Here, you’ll see live, step-by-step updates. You’ll know when it’s “In Transit,” when it’s “Received at the Hub,” and most importantly, when it is “Out for Delivery” (which means it’s sitting in the courier van currently driving around your neighbourhood).

3. What to Do If Your Order Is Late

Even with the best logistics in the country, things occasionally go wrong. A courier van breaks down, bad weather causes delays, or there’s a massive spike in order volumes. We know it’s incredibly frustrating when you’re waiting for something as important as healthcare products.

If your Zapmed delivery time has passed (e.g., it’s been two days in Cape Town, or 72 hours in a regional town) and you haven’t received your parcel, don’t panic. Here is exactly what you should do:

Scenario A: You Have Your Waybill Number, But the Tracking Hasn’t Been Updated

Sometimes couriers forget to scan a parcel at a transit hub, making it look like your package is stuck. If your tracking link hasn’t been updated in 24 hours, reach out to our support team. We have direct lines to the depot managers and can usually get an immediate location update for you.

Scenario B: You Lost the Waybill and Only Have an Order Number

This brings us back to our customer quote at the beginning of this post. Life gets busy, emails get deleted, and sometimes you find yourself thinking, “I only have a #ZM-12345 order number, how do I track my order, Zapmed!?”

It is completely okay. Your Zapmed order number is perfectly fine.

  1. Email or WhatsApp our Support Team: Send a quick message to our customer care desk.
  2. Quote your Order Number: Just say, “Hi, I’m checking on order #ZM-12345. I don’t have my waybill.”
  3. Let us do the heavy lifting: Our support agents will look up your profile, retrieve the waybill from our back-end system, check the courier portal on your behalf, and reply with an exact update on where your package is.

We monitor our support channels closely because we know that when it comes to your health, you shouldn’t be left in the dark. We will gladly trace the parcel, contact the courier driver, and ensure your medication gets into your hands as safely and swiftly as possible.

Wrapping Up

Navigating your health online is supposed to make your life easier, not give you more admin to manage. While 99% of our deliveries go off without a hitch, we are always here to step in when a parcel gets delayed. Whether you’re a busy professional in Sandton needing same-day service or a working mom in the Southern Suburbs expecting a next-day drop-off, keeping you informed is our top priority.

If you ever have doubts about your delivery, or if you’ve lost your tracking info, don’t hesitate to reach out. We’ve got your back.

Need to review your current treatment plan, or are you ready to get your health sorted without leaving the house?

Speak to a Zapmed doctor.

[/et_pb_text][/et_pb_column][/et_pb_row][/et_pb_section]

posts.title: How Much Does Mounjaro Cost in South Africa? A Transparent GLP-1 Price Comparison
posts.excerpt: Recently, you've probably heard the buzz around GLP-1 medications—the highly effective weight-loss injections that everyone from Hollywood A-listers to your gym buddy seems to be talking about.
posts.body:
Recently, you’ve probably heard the buzz around GLP-1 medications—the highly effective weight-loss injections that everyone from Hollywood A-listers to your gym buddy seems to be talking about. 

The results are real, but let’s talk about the elephant in the room: the price tag. Navigating the cost of these medications in South Africa can feel a lot like trying to understand your medical aid benefits: confusing, frustrating, and often surprisingly expensive.

If you’re looking into options like Mounjaro or Wegovy for weight loss, you want straight answers, not a clinical brochure. You want to know if it’s going to work, and more importantly, if you can actually afford it month after month.

Let’s break it down so you can make the best choice for your body and your budget.

“I would like to know the costs of your Tirzepatide. I think I need a dose higher than 2 mg per week, and I’m concerned about costs.

We hear this all the time at Zapmed, and it is a completely valid concern. When you are paying out of pocket (because let’s face it, most South African medical aids are still dragging their feet on covering proactive weight-loss treatments), affordability is the deciding factor.

To answer your question plainly: the cost of your medication will depend on which branded option you choose, what dose you require, and how your body responds over time. Both medications on the market require dose escalation, meaning the price you start at is not necessarily the price you’ll stay at.

Table of Contents

  • Mounjaro vs. Wegovy
  • How Much Does Mounjaro Cost in South Africa?Transparent GLP-1 Price Comparison Table
  • Why Does the Price Go Up, Anyway?
  • Putting The Right Plan in Place
  • Which Medication Is Right for You?
  • Ready to Find Your Fit?

Mounjaro vs. Wegovy

To truly understand what you’re paying for, you need to know the main players in the South African GLP-1 market right now.

  • Mounjaro (Tirzepatide – Branded): Distributed by Aspen in SA, this is the current heavyweight champion. It’s a dual-action medication (targeting both GIP and GLP-1 receptors), meaning it often delivers faster and more significant weight-loss results. 
  • Wegovy (Semaglutide – Branded): Manufactured by Novo Nordisk, this targets just the GLP-1 receptor. It’s highly effective, and following some intense local competition earlier this year, Novo Nordisk recently cut its prices in South Africa. This made the starting doses much more competitive.

How Much Does Mounjaro Cost in South Africa?Transparent GLP-1 Price Comparison Table

Here is exactly what you can expect to pay in South Africa right now. We’ve included the dose-escalation pricing so you aren’t hit with any nasty surprises when it’s time to up your dose in month three.

(Note: Branded pharmacy prices can fluctuate depending on dispensing fees. These figures are realistic estimates based on the South African market as of April 2026).

Both medications are now SAHPRA-approved, dispensed through licensed pharmacies, and backed by extensive clinical trial data. The choice between them comes down to your biology, your weight-loss goals, and your budget.

Why Does the Price Go Up, Anyway?

If you’re new to the world of GLP-1s, you might be wondering why you can’t just buy one dose and stick with it forever. It all comes down to how these medications interact with your body.

To minimise side effects like nausea or fatigue, you have to start on a very low dose, essentially letting your system get used to the medication. Over several weeks or months, your doctor will gradually “escalate” or increase your dose until you reach the optimal therapeutic level for consistent weight loss.

With branded pens or vials, a higher concentration of the drug usually means a higher price. This is where many women hit a wall. You start seeing amazing results on the lower dose; your clothes are fitting better, and your energy is up, but when it’s time to move to the dose that will sustain that progress, the cost becomes a serious consideration.

  • READ MORE: Four Key Differences Between Wegovy and Mounjaro for Medical Weight Loss in South Africa

Individuals who tested positive, but whose partners have not yet been tested

If someone you have been intimate with recently received a positive diagnosis, you may need to be assessed even if you feel well. Many STIs present without symptoms for extended periods. Online platforms can help you request a test kit, assess your risk in consultation with a practitioner, and begin treatment if it is clinically appropriate to do so before your results come. 

Individuals with classic symptoms who have not been tested

Some STI symptoms are textbook clear: an unusual discharge, a burning sensation during urination, sores in the genital area, or an unexpected rash. Experienced clinicians recognise these patterns without needing a laboratory result to begin treatment. They can assess your symptoms via an online consultation and, where appropriate, prescribe syndromic management. You already have the evidence. Your online doctor reviews it and acts on it. It is one of the most straightforward use cases for this kind of service.

Individuals with high anxiety around medical settings

Medical anxiety is a legitimate and widespread condition. 

For some people, the idea of sitting in a clinic, discussing intimate health issues face-to-face with a stranger in a white coat, or being examined physically, is enough to make them avoid healthcare entirely. 

This avoidance can allow treatable infections to progress into more serious complications. Online STI treatment offers a clinical service without the environmental triggers that cause anxiety, making it far more likely that these individuals will follow through on getting the help they need.

Individuals who value strict confidentiality

Some people simply require a higher level of privacy than a standard clinic visit provides. Public figures, professionals in high-profile roles, individuals in conservative communities, or anyone who worries about being seen, hold legitimate concerns about confidentiality.

Frequently asked questions about online STI treatment in South Africa

What are the 7 common STIs in South Africa?

In South Africa, research consistently highlights a group of sexually transmitted infections that appear most often in clinics and testing data. These include chlamydia, gonorrhoea, syphilis, HIV, genital herpes, human papillomavirus (HPV), and trichomoniasis. Some of these are bacterial infections, which are usually treatable with medication, while others are viral and managed over time. Because several of them can exist without obvious symptoms, regular testing plays a big role in staying healthy.

What are 5 symptoms of an STI?

STIs do not always cause symptoms, which is why testing is so important. When symptoms do appear, they often include unusual discharge from the penis or vagina, pain or burning during urination, sores or bumps in the genital area, itching or irritation, and lower abdominal pain. In some cases, people may also notice bleeding between periods or pain during sex. If anything feels off, it is worth getting checked.

How can I treat an STI on my own?

It’s important to be clear here: treating an STI on your own without proper medical guidance is not recommended. Many STIs require specific antibiotics or antiviral medication, and using the wrong treatment can make things worse or delay recovery. What you can do is take the first step yourself by seeking an online consultation or visiting a clinic. A healthcare provider can assess your symptoms and prescribe the correct treatment safely.

Can an STI naturally go away?

Some symptoms of an STI may fade over time, but that does not mean the infection is gone. Infections like chlamydia or gonorrhoea can continue to damage the body even if symptoms disappear. Others, like herpes or HIV, remain in the body and need ongoing management. Relying on an STI to “go away” on its own can lead to complications and increase the risk of spreading it to others.

How long does an STI take to heal?

The healing time depends on the type of infection and how quickly treatment starts. Bacterial STIs like chlamydia and gonorrhoea often improve within a few days after starting antibiotics, though you usually complete a full course over about a week. Viral infections such as herpes may improve within a couple of weeks during an outbreak, but the virus stays in the body. Following treatment instructions carefully helps ensure proper recovery.

What STIs can be treated online?

Many common STIs can be assessed and treated through online healthcare services. A doctor will ask detailed questions about your symptoms, medical history, and possible exposure, and may recommend testing before prescribing treatment. Online care is a convenient first step, but in-person visits are still important if symptoms are severe or unclear.

posts.title: 3 Life Stages When a Sexual Health Screening for Couples is Most Important
posts.excerpt: Sexual health is a shared responsibility in any relationship, and screenings are not just for when something feels wrong. For couples, getting tested together builds trust.
posts.body:
Sexual health is a shared responsibility in any relationship, and screenings are not just for when something feels wrong. For couples, getting tested together builds trust, protects both partners, and opens honest conversations about wellbeing. Knowing when to prioritise these screenings is just as important as doing them at all. There are three key life stages where a couple’s sexual health screening is especially valuable.

Table of Contents

  • When You Become Exclusive
  • When trying to conceive or during pregnancy planning
  • During perimenopause and midlife transitions
  • Conclusion
  • Frequently asked questions about an STI screening
    • How do I know if I have an STI?
    • What is considered a full STD test?
    • What happens at a full sexual health screening?
    • How do I know if a person has an STI?

When You Become Exclusive

The transition from casual dating to a committed relationship is one of the most important moments to get screened together. 

Both partners bring a sexual history into a new relationship, and neither person should assume they are carrying nothing of concern. 

Many sexually transmitted infections, including chlamydia, gonorrhoea, and even HIV, can be completely symptom-free for months or years. 

Getting a full panel together before stopping other forms of protection creates a clean, honest foundation. 

It also normalises the conversation around sexual health early in the relationship, which makes future discussions far easier.

When trying to conceive or during pregnancy planning

Preconception and early pregnancy are crucial times for sexual health screening. 

Some infections can affect fertility, while others can be passed to a baby during pregnancy or childbirth. 

Screening allows for early treatment, reducing risks to both the parent and the child. For example, untreated infections can lead to complications such as pelvic inflammatory disease or increase the chances of pregnancy-related issues. 

Even in long-term relationships, this step is important because infections can remain undetected for years. Couples who screen before trying to conceive are taking a proactive approach to their future family’s health.

  • READ MORE: The Shocking Truth About STIs and Infertility

During perimenopause and midlife transitions

Many people are surprised to learn that STI rates among adults over 45 have been rising in recent years. Hormonal changes during perimenopause can cause vaginal thinning and dryness, which increases susceptibility to infection. Midlife also brings relationship changes, including separation, divorce, or new partnerships, that may reintroduce sexual health risks many people associate only with youth. Routine screening during this stage is just as important as it was in early adulthood, yet it is far less discussed. Normalising screening at midlife removes stigma and catches infections that might otherwise go undetected for years.

Conclusion

Sexual health is a shared responsibility, and for couples, getting screened together can strengthen trust, prevent transmission of infections, and support long-term well-being.

If you or your partner has tested positive or is showing symptoms, you do not need to navigate treatment alone or in person. You can book an online consultation with a Zapmed doctor, who will assess your situation, prescribe the appropriate STI treatment, and have it delivered discreetly to your door.

Frequently asked questions about an STI screening

How do I know if I have an STI?

The tricky part about sexually transmitted infections is that many don’t cause obvious symptoms — especially in the early stages. That means you can feel completely fine and still have an infection.

When symptoms do show up, they can include:

  • Unusual discharge from the penis or vagina
  • Burning or pain when urinating
  • Sores, bumps, or rashes in the genital area
  • Itching or irritation
  • Pain during sex
  • Lower abdominal pain (especially in women)

However, infections like Chlamydia and Gonorrhoea are often “silent”. The only reliable way to know your status is to get tested — not to wait for symptoms.

What is considered a full STD test?

A “full” STD test isn’t always a single standard panel — it can vary slightly depending on your risk factors, sexual history, and symptoms. But in most cases, a comprehensive screen includes testing for:

  • HIV
  • Syphilis
  • Chlamydia
  • Gonorrhoea

In some cases, testing may also include:

  • Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C
  • Herpes simplex virus (if symptoms are present)
  • Human papillomavirus (typically via cervical screening in women)

A proper “full” test is tailored, not one-size-fits-all.

What happens at a full sexual health screening?

A full screening is straightforward and usually quick. It typically includes:

1. A confidential consultation

A healthcare provider will ask about your sexual history, symptoms, and any potential exposure. This helps determine which tests are appropriate.

2. Sample collection

Depending on what’s being tested, this may include:

  • A blood sample (for HIV, syphilis, hepatitis)
  • A urine sample (commonly for chlamydia and gonorrhoea)
  • Swabs (genital, throat, or rectal, depending on sexual practices)

3. Physical examination (if needed)

Only done if you have symptoms like sores, discharge, or pain.

4. Results and treatment plan

Some results come back within minutes (like rapid HIV tests), while others take a few days. Many bacterial STIs are easily treated with antibiotics. Viral infections are managed with medication and monitoring.

How do I know if a person has an STI?

You usually can’t tell just by looking at someone. Most people with an STI have no visible signs.

Even if someone appears healthy:

  • They may not know they’re infected.
  • They may have no symptoms yet.
  • Symptoms may come and go.

The only way to know someone’s status is through recent, verified testing — and even then, timing matters because of “window periods” (the time between exposure and when a test can detect an infection).

That’s why open conversations, regular testing, and protection (like condoms) are key, not assumptions based on appearance or trust alone.

posts.title: 4 Common Myths About Hair Loss Treatment in South Africa
posts.excerpt: Hair loss treatment in South Africa is often misunderstood, leading to frustration and poor decisions. The most effective approach is early action, evidence-based treatment, and realistic expectations.
posts.body:
Hair loss treatment in South Africa is often misunderstood, leading to frustration and poor decisions. The most effective approach is early action, evidence-based treatment, and realistic expectations. Understanding what is fact versus fiction is the first step toward seeing results for hair regrowth.

Table of Contents

  • Myth 1: Hair Loss Is Only a Men’s Problem
  • Myth 2: Only Expensive Treatments Work
  • Myth 3: Natural Remedies Are Just as Effective as Medical Treatment
  • Myth 4: Hair Loss Treatment Produces Instant Results
  • Frequently asked questions about hair loss
    • What helps with hair loss?
    • How can I stop hair loss permanently?
    • How can I stop hair loss and regrow hair naturally?
    • How do I stop my hair from falling out and thinning?
    • How much does hair loss treatment cost in South Africa?
    • What are the major causes of hair loss?
    • Does Vaseline grow hair?
    • What vitamin am I lacking if my hair is falling out?
    • What is the miracle cure for hair loss?
    • Can minoxidil stop chemo hair loss?
    • What are minoxidil’s side effects?
    • How to grow hair faster naturally in a week?

Myth 1: Hair Loss Is Only a Men’s Problem

One of the most pervasive myths is that hair loss exclusively affects men. 

In reality, millions of South African women experience significant hair thinning and loss, particularly due to conditions like traction alopecia — a form of hair loss caused by tight hairstyles such as braids, weaves, and extensions that are deeply embedded in local beauty culture. 

Female pattern hair loss is also widely underdiagnosed because many women assume their shedding is “normal” or temporary. 

The truth is that hair loss does not discriminate by gender, and women deserve the same access to diagnosis and treatment.

Myth 2: Only Expensive Treatments Work

Many South Africans believe that effective hair loss treatment is reserved for those who can afford premium clinics or imported products. 

This simply isn’t true. 

Clinically proven, affordable options such as minoxidil, available over the counter at most South African pharmacies, have decades of research supporting their effectiveness for both men and women. 

  • READ MORE: Do Hair Loss Shampoos Work?

Myth 3: Natural Remedies Are Just as Effective as Medical Treatment

South Africa has a rich tradition of natural healing, and while many herbal remedies serve important cultural and wellness roles, they are not equivalent to clinically proven treatments for hair loss. 

Products containing minoxidil or finasteride have decades of peer-reviewed research supporting their effectiveness. 

Rubbing onion juice, castor oil, or egg white on your scalp may not harm you, but for significant hair loss caused by genetics or hormonal changes, these remedies will not stop the underlying process. 

Natural options can support scalp health, but they should not replace a proper diagnosis and treatment plan.

Myth 4: Hair Loss Treatment Produces Instant Results

Another myth is the expectation of quick results, a belief aggressively fuelled by social media advertisements promising dramatic transformations in weeks. 

In reality, most clinically approved treatments require consistent use for at least three to six months before any visible improvement appears. 

Hair growth is a slow biological process, and patience is essential. Stopping treatment prematurely because results aren’t immediate is one of the leading reasons people in South Africa conclude that “nothing works” — when in fact they simply didn’t give the treatment sufficient time.

Frequently asked questions about hair loss

What helps with hair loss?

What works depends on the cause. The most evidence-backed treatment is minoxidil, which helps prolong the growth phase of hair. If hair loss is hormonal (like pattern baldness), doctors may also prescribe finasteride for men.

Beyond medication, basics matter: enough protein, managing stress, and treating scalp conditions like dandruff can all make a difference.

How can I stop hair loss permanently?

In most cases, you can’t “permanently” stop hair loss—especially genetic hair loss. Conditions like androgenetic alopecia are ongoing, which means treatment needs to be ongoing too.

The goal is control, not cure: slow the loss, maintain what you have, and regrow where possible.

How can I stop hair loss and regrow hair naturally?

Natural approaches can support hair health, but they’re usually not strong enough alone for significant regrowth. Focus on:

  • Adequate protein intake
  • Iron and vitamin levels
  • Gentle hair care (avoid tight styles, harsh chemicals)
  • Stress reduction

If follicles are shrinking, you’ll likely still need medical treatment alongside these habits.

How do I stop my hair from falling out and thinning?

Start by identifying the cause. Common triggers include stress, illness, hormonal changes, and nutritional deficiencies.

A doctor may diagnose conditions like telogen effluvium, which often resolves once the trigger is addressed. Early treatment is key—waiting usually leads to more noticeable thinning.

How much does hair loss treatment cost in South Africa?

Costs vary depending on the approach:

  • Minoxidil: roughly R150–R400 per month depending on brand
  • Doctor consultation: ±R300–R800 privately

Telehealth platforms like Zapmed offer a more predictable option:

  • Subscription: R220/month
  • Plus, medication costs monthly.

This can make ongoing treatment easier to manage, especially since hair loss treatment is long-term.

What are the major causes of hair loss?

The most common causes include:

  • Genetics (pattern hair loss)
  • Hormonal changes (thyroid, postpartum)
  • Stress or illness
  • Nutrient deficiencies (iron, protein)
  • Certain medications
  • Medical conditions like alopecia areata

Does Vaseline grow hair?

No. Petroleum jelly can help lock in moisture and protect hair from breakage, but it doesn’t stimulate hair growth or affect the hair follicle.

What vitamin am I lacking if my hair is falling out?

Hair loss is often linked to:

  • Iron deficiency
  • Vitamin D deficiency
  • Low B12
  • Zinc deficiency

But don’t guess—blood tests are the best way to confirm before supplementing.

What is the miracle cure for hair loss?

There isn’t one. If something claims instant regrowth or a “miracle cure”, it’s not evidence-based. Real treatments take months and require consistency.

Can minoxidil stop chemo hair loss?

No. Chemotherapy targets rapidly dividing cells, including hair follicles. Minoxidil may help speed up regrowth after treatment, but it doesn’t prevent hair loss during chemo.

What are minoxidil’s side effects?

Most people tolerate it well, but possible side effects include:

  • Scalp irritation or itching
  • Dryness or flaking
  • Temporary shedding when starting (this is normal)
  • Unwanted facial hair (rare, more common in women)

Serious side effects are uncommon when used correctly.

How to grow hair faster naturally in a week?

You can’t meaningfully speed up hair growth in a week. Hair grows about 1–1.5 cm per month.

What you can do is optimise conditions:

  • Eat enough protein
  • Avoid heat and tight styles
  • Keep your scalp healthy

Real growth improvements show over months, not days.

posts.title: Four Key Differences Between Wegovy and Mounjaro for Medical Weight Loss in South Africa
posts.excerpt: Obesity treatment in South Africa doesn't look the way it did ten years ago. The conversation about weight—long dominated by diets, willpower, and shame—now often ends with a prescription.
posts.body:
Obesity treatment in South Africa doesn’t look the way it did ten years ago. The conversation about weight—long dominated by diets, willpower, and shame—now often ends with a prescription, if medically suitable. More people are asking their doctors about Wegovy and Mounjaro for weight management. And yes, more doctors are having that conversation back.

Both are once-weekly injectable medications that help regulate appetite and support weight loss. But are they the same thing? Which one is better? What’s the real difference? Here’s a breakdown of four ways they compare, so you can walk into that doctor’s consultation better informed.

Table of Contents

  • How They Work: One Hormone vs Two
  • Weight Loss Results: What the Trials Show
  • Approval Status in South Africa
  • Medical Aid Coverage: What You Can Expect
  • Frequently asked questions about Wegvy vs Mounjaro
    • What is the best medication for weight loss in South Africa?
    • What is similar to Ozempic in South Africa?
    • What is the generic name for Mounjaro?
    • How much does the Mounjaro injection cost in South Africa? 
    • Are medical weight loss treatments covered by South African medical aid?

How They Work: One Hormone vs Two

GLP-1 is a natural hormone your gut releases after a meal. It tells your brain you’re satisfied and keeps blood sugar stable. Wegovy is a medication that mimics this hormone to help with weight loss. Mounjaro does the same but also targets a second hormone called GIP. GIP works alongside GLP-1 to boost insulin and enhance appetite control in a complementary way. Together, they create a stronger signal to the body to store less fat.

This explains why some patients achieve greater weight loss with Mounjaro compared with Wegovy under medical care. A healthcare provider will decide the best option after review of the medical history and expected treatment response.

Weight Loss Results: What the Trials Show

Clinical trials and head-to-head studies have indicated that Mounjaro is more efficient for weight loss than Wegovy.

In the SURMOUNT-5 trial, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in May 2025, participants on Mounjaro lost an average of 20.2% of their body weight over 72 weeks, compared to 13.7% on Wegovy. However, a higher dose of Wegovy (7.2 mg) studied in the 2025 STEP UP trial showed that adults with obesity lost around 21% of body weight over the same period. At standard doses, Mounjaro leads. At the newer, higher Wegovy dose, the gap narrows considerably.

Approval Status in South Africa

Wegovy launched in South Africa in August 2025 and is the first GLP-1 medication formally approved here for weight management. Mounjaro launched in December 2024 as a diabetes treatment, and SAHPRA only gave it the green light for weight loss in October 2025. So for a period, doctors who prescribed Mounjaro for weight loss were doing so “off-label” — outside its official, approved purpose. Both now hold full approval for weight management in South Africa.

Medical Aid Coverage: What You Can Expect

Mounjaro has official registration for both diabetes and weight loss in South Africa, so schemes may cover it under the Chronic Illness Benefit — but only for members with type 2 diabetes who meet strict clinical criteria. Wegovy is registered solely for weight management, and because obesity is not classified as a Prescribed Minimum Benefit condition, schemes are not obligated to cover it. Members must either pay out of pocket or use their Savings Benefit, if available on their plan.

Frequently asked questions about Wegvy vs Mounjaro

What is the best medication for weight loss in South Africa?

There is no single “best” medication for everyone, but two leading options are Wegovy (semaglutide) and Mounjaro (tirzepatide). Wegovy is specifically approved for weight loss in South Africa and typically leads to around 15–20% body weight reduction when combined with lifestyle changes.

Mounjaro is often considered more potent because it targets two hormones (GLP-1 and GIP), which may result in greater weight loss in some patients, although it is sometimes prescribed off-label for weight management.

In practice, the “best” option depends on your BMI, medical history, cost, and whether you also have type 2 diabetes.

What is similar to Ozempic in South Africa?

The closest equivalent to Ozempic is Wegovy, as both contain the same active ingredient, semaglutide. The difference is that Wegovy is formulated at higher doses and is specifically approved for weight loss, while Ozempic is approved for diabetes but may be prescribed off-label for weight loss.

Another alternative is Mounjaro, which works differently but produces similar or greater weight-loss effects due to its dual-hormone action.

What is the generic name for Mounjaro?

The generic name for Mounjaro is tirzepatide, a dual GLP-1 and GIP receptor agonist used to regulate appetite, blood sugar, and metabolism.

How much does the Mounjaro injection cost in South Africa? 

The cost of Mounjaro in South Africa varies depending on dosage and provider. Typical pricing ranges from about R3,600 to R8,100 per month, with many patients paying around R4,000 to R4,600 monthly for standard doses.

Some structured programmes offer lower entry pricing, starting from roughly R2,500 to R5,100 per month, depending on support and dosage.

Zapmed’s cost starts from R1940 cash (R799 service fee plus medication starting point price).

Our subscription service is available from R1410 per month, cash (R450 subscription fee plus the medication’s starting point price).

Are medical weight loss treatments covered by South African medical aid?

Generally, no. Medical aids do not usually cover GLP-1 medications for weight loss, because obesity is not classified as a Prescribed Minimum Benefit (PMB).

Some schemes may cover these medications only for type 2 diabetes, and often under strict conditions.

The National Library of Medicine projects that around 150 million men worldwide are living with erectile dysfunction (ED). It is a figure that reflects the scale of this condition. It is also a reminder that no man dealing with it is navigating unfamiliar territory. Doctors see this regularly, treat it regularly, and understand it well.

Men’s willingness to engage with the subject has grown. Where the conversation was once largely avoided, it is now something men are raising with their doctors, researching thoughtfully, and managing as they would any other health condition. That change in approach has had a positive effect on outcomes.

The practical side of accessing care has also improved. Telehealth has made it possible for men to consult with qualified professionals from home, receive a prescription if appropriate, and manage their treatment privately. 

For many, this removes the main hesitation that previously kept them from seeking help in the first place.

Before beginning erectile dysfunction treatment, we wanted to give you a breakdown of what to expect. Here are five key things men in South Africa should know as they take that first step.

Table of Contents

  • What is erectile dysfunction?
  • What to expect when starting erectile dysfunction treatment

    • There might be an adjustment period

What is erectile dysfunction?

Erectile dysfunction is a consistent inability to get or keep an erection firm enough for sex. 

It usually comes down to blood flow: conditions like diabetes, heart disease, and high blood pressure can interfere with circulation in ways that affect erections directly. 

Stress, anxiety, and depression are equally capable of causing ED and tend to be underestimated. Low testosterone is another factor that often comes up. On the lifestyle side, smoking, drinking heavily, carrying excess weight, and being inactive all increase the risk. 

ED becomes more common as men get older, but age is not the defining factor it is often assumed to be. Once the cause is identified, treatment makes a meaningful difference to sexual function.

What to expect when starting erectile dysfunction treatment

Treatment requires a thorough medical assessment

Starting treatment for erectile dysfunction usually begins with a detailed consultation. A doctor will ask about your symptoms, lifestyle, stress levels, and overall health. They may also review medications you’re currently taking and check for underlying conditions like type 2 diabetes or hypertension, which commonly affect sexual function. This step ensures treatment is safe, appropriate, and targeted to the root cause rather than just the symptoms.

Treatment is personalised to the patient

There’s no single treatment that works for everyone with erectile dysfunction. Your doctor will look at the root cause and your overall health before deciding whether medication, counselling, lifestyle changes, or a mix of approaches makes the most sense. It’s common for the treatment plan to change slightly over time as your doctor learns how your body responds.

Medication is not an “instant on” switch

A common misconception fuelled by pop culture is that taking a pill leads to an immediate, uncontrollable erection. In reality, modern ED medications require sexual arousal to work. They function by enhancing the natural chemical signals sent during stimulation, making it easier for blood to flow into the chamber. You should expect to still engage in foreplay and psychological intimacy; the treatment provides physiological assistance, but the spark must still come from you.

There might be an adjustment period

Results are not always immediate. Some treatments work quickly, while others take time to show consistent improvement. Your body may need a few attempts to respond as expected, especially with medication. It’s normal to have mixed results at first, and follow-up appointments help refine the approach if needed.

Treatment might address the psychological component

Even if the root cause of ED is physical, there is almost always a psychological layer involved. Performance anxiety can create a self-fulfilling prophecy: the fear of “failing” triggers a stress response that constricts blood vessels, making an erection more difficult to achieve even with medication.

There might be necessary lifestyle adjustments

Medication is often more effective when supported by healthy habits. Your doctor will likely discuss lifestyle changes that improve vascular health. Expect recommendations to:

  • Improve Diet: Focusing on heart-healthy foods.
  • Increase Activity: Exercise improves circulation and testosterone levels.
  • Limit Substances: Reducing alcohol and nicotine intake, both of which are major contributors to erectile issues.

By viewing treatment as a lifestyle shift rather than just a pill, you increase the likelihood of sustainable, long-term improvement.

Expect some possible side effects

Like any medical treatment, ED therapies can come with side effects. These are usually mild and may include headaches, flushing, nasal congestion, or dizziness, depending on the medication. Most side effects settle as your body adjusts, but it is important to report anything unusual to your doctor so adjustments can be made safely.

A realistic timeline of ED treatment

For most people, ED treatment works on different timelines depending on the approach. Oral medications such as sildenafil or tadalafil can start working within 15–60 minutes, but only when taken before sex and with stimulation. Consistent improvement may take a few attempts or dose adjustments over several weeks. Lifestyle changes or psychological therapy typically take weeks to months to show benefits. Long-term outcomes vary, but many treatments remain effective with ongoing use under medical guidance.

Frequently asked questions about erectile dysfunction treatment

What medication is used for erectile dysfunction in South Africa?

In South Africa, the most commonly prescribed medications for erectile dysfunction are phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5) inhibitors such as sildenafil (the active ingredient in Viagra), tadalafil (Cialis), and vardenafil. These medicines work by improving blood flow to the penis, making it easier to achieve and maintain an erection when sexually stimulated. A doctor will usually recommend one based on your health profile, how long you want the effect to last, and how often you plan to use it.

What is the permanent cure for erectile dysfunction?

There isn’t a single permanent cure for erectile dysfunction, because the condition often has underlying causes such as cardiovascular disease, diabetes, stress, or hormonal imbalances. Treatment focuses on addressing those root issues alongside symptom relief. In some cases, improving overall health, adjusting medication, or treating psychological factors can significantly reduce or even resolve symptoms over time.

Can a man recover from erectile dysfunction?

Many men do recover from erectile dysfunction, especially when the cause is identified early and managed properly. Lifestyle changes such as regular exercise, better sleep, reduced alcohol intake, and quitting smoking can make a difference. Where psychological factors play a role, counselling or therapy can help. For others, ongoing treatment may be needed, but it can still be highly effective and allow for a normal sex life.

In South Africa, you cannot legally get Viagra or similar erectile dysfunction tablets without a doctor’s prescription. These medications require medical oversight to ensure they are safe for you, especially if you have underlying health conditions or take other medications that could interact with them.

What are the potential side effects of common ED tablets?

Common side effects of ED tablets are generally mild and temporary. They can include headaches, facial flushing, nasal congestion, dizziness, and indigestion. Some men also report back pain or muscle aches, particularly with longer-acting options like tadalafil. Rare but serious side effects, such as changes in vision or prolonged erections, require immediate medical attention, which is why proper medical guidance is important before starting treatment.

A consultation from home, on a lunch break or before school drop-off, with a qualified doctor who can refer, prescribe, and follow up, even after hours (evenings and weekends).

6 Tips to prepare for your first online doctor consultation 

Conduct a technical rehearsal

Even if you are tech-savvy, various platforms have different requirements for microphone and camera permissions. Ten minutes before your appointment, log in to ensure your internet connection is stable and your device is fully charged. A pair of headphones with a built-in microphone will usually offer clearer audio and more privacy than your device’s internal speakers.

Optimise your environment

Find a quiet, private space where you won’t be interrupted. Lighting is particularly important for medical calls. Ensure the light source is in front of you rather than behind you. This allows the GP to see your face and skin tone clearly, which can be a vital diagnostic tool, especially if you are discussing symptoms like rashes or inflammation.

Summarise your primary concerns

Virtual consultations often move faster than in-person visits. Write down a brief list of your symptoms, when they started, and any specific questions you have. If you keep these points in front of you, you can avoid “blanking” once the camera turns on and stay focused on your highest-priority concerns.

Have vital signs ready

If you have basic medical equipment at home, such as a thermometer, a blood pressure cuff, or a wearable fitness tracker that monitors heart rate, keep them nearby. Recent objective data, like a temperature reading or resting heart rate, adds a necessary layer of clinical accuracy to a remote conversation.

Keep a pen and notebook handy

While it is tempting to rely on your memory, the GP may provide specific instructions regarding dosages, lifestyle adjustments, or follow-up steps. Jotting these down by hand is often faster and less distracting than trying to type notes on the same screen you’re using for the video call.

Be ready for a remote assessment

Your doctor may guide you through simple checks, like pressing on an area, checking your pulse, or describing symptoms in specific ways. Follow instructions carefully and ask for clarification if needed — this replaces parts of the physical exam.

Have photos or documents ready to upload

Many telehealth platforms let you upload images or documents before or during the consultation. If your condition changes over time, having photos taken earlier can help provide context. The same applies to lab results or reports that support your current concern.

Understand digital follow-ups

Prescriptions, sick notes, and referrals are usually sent electronically via email, SMS, or platform download. Confirm how and when you’ll receive them, and check your inbox (including spam). If medication is prescribed, ask how it will be fulfilled — delivery or pharmacy collection.

Booking a telehealth appointment means the freedom to speak with a qualified doctor from wherever you are. posts.title: Winter Skin Woes? How to Keep Your Skin Hydrated & Healthy in Cold Weather
posts.excerpt: As the temperatures drop and we swap iced lattes for hot chocolate, there's one thing many of us forget—our skin needs extra love during winter.
posts.body:
As the temperatures drop and we swap iced lattes for hot chocolate, there’s one thing many of us forget—our skin needs extra love during winter. 

Cold weather, indoor heating, and dry air can strip moisture from your skin, leaving it feeling tight, flaky, and irritated. If your once-glowy complexion is looking a little… well, dull and dehydrated, don’t stress. The right winter skincare routine and a few dry skin remedies can bring it back to life!

So, let’s break down why your skin struggles in winter, how to protect your moisture barrier, and the best moisturizer for dry skin that will have you glowing all season long.

1. Why Does Skin Get So Dry in Winter?

Winter sucks the moisture right out of your skin—and here’s why:

 📌 Cold air = less humidity – Dry air outside means your skin loses moisture faster.
 📌 Indoor heating = dehydrated skin – Heaters and air conditioning strip moisture from the air (and your face).
 📌 Hot showers = bad news – Steamy water feels amazing but can damage your skin barrier.
 📌 Harsh winds = irritation – Wind exposure can cause redness, flakiness, and sensitivity.

💡 The result? Your skin loses hydration faster than it can retain it, leading to dull, flaky, irritated skin.

2. Signs Your Skin Needs More Hydration

How do you know if your skin is crying out for help? Look out for these winter skin SOS signs:

🚨 Tight, rough, or flaky skin
 🚨 Itching or irritation (especially on your face & hands)
 🚨 Fine lines looking more noticeable (dehydrated skin = more visible wrinkles!)
 🚨 Dull complexion (skin looks tired, not radiant)
 🚨 Breakouts & sensitivity (dryness can cause oil overproduction, leading to pimples)

💡 If your skin feels like sandpaper instead of silk, it’s time to switch up your routine.

3. Your Ultimate Winter Skincare Routine

If your summer skincare routine is still in rotation, it’s time to upgrade for winter. A hydrating, barrier-supporting routine is your best friend during cold months.

🌞 Morning Routine: Protect & Hydrate

1️⃣ Gentle Cream Cleanser – Ditch foaming cleansers that strip moisture; go for a hydrating, non-stripping cleanser.
 2️⃣ Hydrating Serum (Hyaluronic Acid) – This locks in moisture and plumps up the skin.
 3️⃣ Rich Moisturizer – Look for ingredients like ceramides, glycerin, and squalane.
 4️⃣ SPF (Yes, Even in Winter!) – UV rays still damage your skin, even on cloudy days.

🌙 Night Routine: Repair & Lock in Moisture

1️⃣ Double Cleanse (If Wearing Makeup or SPF) – Use a cleansing balm + gentle face wash.
 2️⃣ Exfoliate (2x a Week Max) – Use a gentle chemical exfoliant (like lactic acid) to remove dead skin.
 3️⃣ Barrier-Repairing Serum (Niacinamide or Peptides) – Helps strengthen your skin barrier.
 4️⃣ Ultra-Rich Moisturizer or Overnight Mask – Go for a thicker, more nourishing formula at night.
 5️⃣ Lip Balm & Hand Cream – Your lips and hands need love too!

💡 Pro Tip: Use a humidifier in your bedroom to stop your skin from drying out overnight.

 

4. Best Moisturizer for Dry Skin in Winter

Not all moisturizers are created equal—some work better for dry winter skin than others.

Look for these ingredients:
 ✔ Hyaluronic Acid – Binds moisture to the skin.
 ✔ Glycerin – Acts as a humectant to pull in water.
 ✔ Ceramides – Strengthen your skin’s protective barrier.
 ✔ Shea Butter & Squalane – Intensely hydrating & nourishing.
 ✔ Niacinamide – Helps repair damaged, sensitive skin.

💡 The best winter moisturizers are THICKER and contain a mix of humectants (hydrators) and occlusives (barrier protectors).

 

5. Dry Skin Remedies That Actually Work

Aside from a solid skincare routine, small changes in your daily habits can make a HUGE difference.

✅ Switch to lukewarm showers – Hot water strips skin’s natural oils.
 ✅ Apply moisturizer to damp skin – Locks in hydration better.
 ✅ Drink more water – Hydrated skin starts from within.
 ✅ Use hydrating face masks – Once or twice a week for extra nourishment.
 ✅ Wear gloves & scarves – Protect your skin from cold winds.

💡 Skincare isn’t just about products—it’s about your habits too!

 

6. The Bottom Line: Hydration = Winter Glow-Up

Winter weather can wreak havoc on your skin, but the right skincare routine and habits can keep it soft, hydrated, and healthy. Swap to richer products, hydrate like your glow depends on it, and protect your skin barrier. 

#WinterSkinCare #HydrateAndGlow #ColdWeatherBeauty

posts.title: Why Your Gut Health Matters & How It Affects Your Skin, Mood & More
posts.excerpt: You know that "gut feeling" people always talk about? Turns out, it's not just a figure of speech—your gut health literally affects everything.
posts.body:
You know that “gut feeling” people always talk about? Turns out, it’s not just a figure of speech—your gut health literally affects everything, from your skin to your mood and even your energy levels.

If you’ve been dealing with digestive issues, stubborn acne, brain fog, or feeling meh all the time, your gut might be trying to tell you something. This week, let’s talk about the gut-brain connection, how gut health and skin are linked, and why probiotics for wellness might just be your new best friend.

1. Gut Health 101: Why It’s a Big Deal

Your gut isn’t just responsible for digestion—it’s like mission control for your entire body.

 📌 70% of your immune system lives in your gut.
 📌 Your gut produces 95% of your serotonin (your “happy” hormone).
 📌 An unhealthy gut can trigger skin breakouts, bloating, anxiety, and inflammation.

Your gut is home to trillions of bacteria, known as your gut microbiome. Some are good (probiotics), some are bad, but when they’re balanced, everything runs smoothly. When they’re out of balance? That’s when problems start.

💡 Think of your gut like a garden. If you feed it well and take care of it, it thrives. But if bad bacteria take over, everything wilts—including your skin and mood.

 

2. The Gut-Brain Connection: Your Second Brain

Ever had stress give you a stomachache? Or noticed how anxiety makes your digestion all kinds of messy? That’s the gut-brain connection in action.

Your gut and brain constantly communicate through the vagus nerve, and when your gut is out of balance, it can mess with your mental health, mood, and even sleep.

🚨 Signs of an Unhappy Gut-Brain Connection:
 ❌ Frequent bloating or constipation
 ❌ Feeling anxious or overwhelmed for no reason
 ❌ Brain fog or difficulty concentrating
 ❌ Mood swings & irritability
 ❌ Poor sleep or constant fatigue

💡 Your mental health isn’t just in your head—it starts in your gut.

 

3. Gut Health & Skin: The Secret to a Natural Glow

Struggling with acne, rosacea, or dull skin that won’t clear up? The answer might not be in your skincare routine—it could be in your gut.

✨ How Gut Health Affects Skin:

✔ Leaky gut = inflamed skin – When your gut lining is damaged, toxins leak into your bloodstream and trigger skin issues like acne, eczema, and psoriasis.
 ✔ Bad bacteria = breakouts – An unbalanced microbiome can lead to inflammation, clogged pores, and excess oil production.
 ✔ Nutrient absorption = healthy skin – If your gut isn’t absorbing vitamins properly, your skin won’t get the glow-up it deserves.

💡 Your skin is a reflection of what’s happening inside your body. Balance your gut, and your skin will follow.

 

4. Probiotics for Wellness: Your Gut’s BFFs

Probiotics are the good bacteria that keep your gut happy, balanced, and functioning properly. They help with digestion, immunity, mental health, and even skin health.

Where to Get Your Probiotics?

🥑 Food sources:

✔ Yogurt with live cultures
 ✔ Fermented foods like kimchi, sauerkraut, and kefir
 ✔ Miso and kombucha

💊 Supplements:
 If you’re not getting enough from food, a high-quality probiotic supplement can help.

🚨 Pro Tip: Pair probiotics with prebiotics (fiber-rich foods like bananas, garlic, and oats) to help them thrive!

 

5. How to Heal Your Gut & Feel Your Best

If your gut is out of balance, don’t stress—it’s 100% fixable with a few lifestyle changes.

✅ Eat More Fiber – Whole foods, veggies, and whole grains keep your gut bacteria happy.
 ✅ Cut Back on Sugar & Processed Foods – Bad bacteria feed on sugar, leading to inflammation.
 ✅ Drink More Water – Hydration helps digestion and nutrient absorption.
 ✅ Manage Stress – Meditation, deep breathing, and movement help regulate the gut-brain connection.
 ✅ Prioritize Sleep – Your gut repairs itself while you rest, so aim for 7-9 hours a night.

💡 Your gut is like a VIP guest—treat it right, and it’ll keep you glowing, energized, and thriving.

 

6. The Bottom Line: Trust Your Gut (Literally!)

🚨 Your gut health affects way more than just digestion—it impacts your skin, mood, energy, and overall wellness.

✨ Prioritizing gut health = prioritizing your entire well-being. ✨

posts.title: Burnout Is Real: Signs You Need a Break & How to Recharge
posts.excerpt: We've all been there—running on empty, exhausted, and feeling like life is one never-ending to-do list. Between work, responsibilities, relationships, and just trying to keep it all together.
posts.body:
We’ve all been there—running on empty, exhausted, and feeling like life is one never-ending to-do list. Between work, responsibilities, relationships, and just trying to keep it all together, it’s easy to push yourself too hard. But here’s the truth: burnout isn’t just feeling tired—it’s your body and mind screaming for help.

April is the perfect time for a Mental Health & Wellness Reset, and that means prioritizing YOU. So, let’s talk about mental health burnout, how to spot the warning signs, and most importantly, how to recharge before you hit breaking point.

1. What Is Burnout & Why Is It So Common?

Burnout isn’t just stress—it’s chronic stress that hasn’t been managed properly. It happens when you’re mentally, emotionally, and physically drained for an extended period.

Burnout isn’t just about work. It can come from studying, parenting, relationships, caregiving, or even just dealing with life.

It’s a major mental health issue. Studies show that burnout increases your risk of anxiety, depression, and even physical health issues like heart problems and weakened immunity.

Women are more likely to experience burnout. The pressure to “do it all” (career, family, social life) means that women often ignore their own needs until burnout hits hard.

💡 The problem? Many people don’t even realize they’re burnt out until it’s too late.

 

2. Signs You Might Be Experiencing Mental Health Burnout

🚨 Constant exhaustion – No amount of sleep helps, and you wake up feeling just as tired.
 🚨 Zero motivation – Work, socializing, and even hobbies feel draining.
 🚨 Irritability & mood swings – Small things set you off, and you feel frustrated all the time.
 🚨 Brain fog – Struggling to concentrate or remember things? Burnout affects cognitive function.
 🚨 Frequent headaches or body pain – Stress takes a physical toll on your body.
 🚨 Feeling detached – You start emotionally withdrawing from friends, family, and even your goals.

If any of this sounds familiar, it’s time to slow down and reset.

 

3. The Difference Between Burnout & Stress

You might be wondering, “Am I just stressed, or is this actual burnout?”

Here’s how to tell the difference:

Think of stress as a warning light and burnout as a total shutdown. The earlier you catch it, the easier it is to recover.

 

4. How to Recharge & Recover from Burnout

Recovering from burnout takes more than a quick nap or a weekend off—you need real lifestyle changes to reset your mental and physical health.

1️⃣ Set Boundaries & Learn to Say No

You can’t do everything, and that’s okay. Prioritize what truly matters and say “no” to things that drain your energy.

2️⃣ Take a Proper Break

🚫 Not just a quick social media scroll.
 ✅ A real break means disconnecting from work/emails and doing something that truly relaxes you.

💡 Pro Tip: If taking a break makes you feel guilty, you probably need it even more.

3️⃣ Sleep Like Your Health Depends on It (Because It Does)

Burnout destroys sleep quality. Try:

  • No screens an hour before bed
  • A consistent sleep schedule (even on weekends)
  • Breathing exercises to calm the mind

4️⃣ Move Your Body—But Make It Enjoyable

Exercise is one of the best stress management tools, but don’t force yourself into intense workouts if you’re exhausted.

 ✔ Go for a walk in nature
 ✔ Try yoga or stretching
 ✔ Dance to your favorite playlist 💃

💡 The goal? Movement that feels GOOD, not punishing.

5️⃣ Fuel Your Body with the Right Foods

When you’re burnt out, you crave sugar, caffeine, and junk food—but these only make things worse.

Try:
 🍓 Omega-3 rich foods (salmon, flaxseeds) for brain health
 🍵 Green tea instead of excessive coffee
 🥑 Healthy fats for sustained energy

6️⃣ Talk to Someone & Get Support

Burnout isn’t something you have to navigate alone. Whether it’s a friend, family member, or therapist, talking about it helps.

 

5. Online Therapy in South Africa: A Tool for Burnout Recovery

If burnout is affecting your mental health, therapy is one of the best ways to get clarity, support, and real solutions.

✔ Therapy helps you process emotions and set better boundaries.
 ✔ You’ll learn practical tools for stress management.
 ✔ A therapist provides an outside perspective on what’s draining you.

Where to Find Therapy in South Africa

Good news: Therapy is more accessible than ever with online therapy SA options.

 📌 Private therapy clinics – Offer both in-person & virtual consultations.
 📌 Employee wellness programs – Some companies offer therapy benefits!
 📌 Community support groups – Free or low-cost options available.
 📌 Online therapy platforms – Virtual sessions for easy, convenient mental health support.

 Therapy isn’t just for crisis moments—it’s a tool for preventing burnout before it gets worse.

 

Burnout Isn’t a Badge of Honor

Burnout isn’t just “part of life.” You don’t need to push through exhaustion to prove your worth.

Prioritizing your mental health = prioritizing your future. When you take care of yourself, you’re not just surviving—you’re thriving.

So take that break. Set those boundaries. Seek help when you need it. Because your well-being is worth it.

Zapmed is here to help you take control of your health & wellness—because you deserve a life that feels good, not just looks good.

posts.excerpt: Valentine's Day is all about love, romance, and feeling yourself—but let's be real: nothing kills the vibe faster than a pregnancy scare or worrying about your reproductive health.
posts.body:
Valentine’s Day is all about love, romance, and feeling yourself—but let’s be real: nothing kills the vibe faster than a pregnancy scare or worrying about your reproductive health. If you’re thinking about getting on birth control (or switching it up), you’ve come to the right place.

Choosing the right contraceptive isn’t just about avoiding unplanned pregnancy; it’s about taking control of your body, your choices, and your future. Whether you’re in a long-term relationship, casually dating, or focusing on self-love, your contraception should fit your lifestyle and health needs.

So, let’s break down the birth control options available in South Africa, debunk the myths, and help you find your perfect match.

Choosing the Right Birth Zapmedl for You

Finding the best birth control depends on:

  • Do you prefer short-term or long-term contraception?
  • Are you okay with hormones, or do you prefer a hormone-free option?
  • Do you need a method that also regulates your periods or helps with acne?
  • Can you commit to taking a daily pill, or would you rather a set-and-forget option?

If you’re unsure, a quick online consultation with one of our Partner Doctors who can help you choose the best contraceptive method for your body and lifestyle. Let’s explore the most effective birth control options available in South Africa, where to get them, and how to find the best one for you.

1. The Pill (Combined & Progestogen-Only) 💊

Best for: People who want a daily, flexible hormone-based option that also helps regulate periods.

What is it?

The contraceptive pill contains hormones (oestrogen and/or progestin) that prevent ovulation, thin the uterine lining, and thicken cervical mucus—all of which help prevent pregnancy.

Pros & Cons

✅ Pros
Regulates periods and reduces cramps
Can improve acne and hormone balance
Easily reversible if you want to conceive

❌ Cons
Must be taken daily for effectiveness
Doesn’t protect against STIs
May cause nausea, bloating, or mood changes

 

*Available at Zapmed

2. The Patch 🩹

Best for: People who want a hormonal contraceptive without a daily pill.

What is it?

The contraceptive patch is a small skin patch that releases oestrogen and progestin, preventing ovulation. It’s worn on the skin and changed weekly.

Pros & Cons

✅ Pros
No daily pill—just change once a week
Regulates periods and reduces PMS symptoms
Easily reversible

❌ Cons
Can cause skin irritation where applied
Doesn’t protect against STIs
Less effective if you weigh over 90kg

*Available at Zapmed

3. The Vaginal Ring ⭕

Best for: People who want a low-maintenance hormonal contraceptive.

What is it?

The contraceptive ring is a soft, flexible ring inserted into the vagina. It releases oestrogen and progestin to prevent pregnancy and is changed once a month.

Pros & Cons

✅ Pros
Once-a-month maintenance
Regulates menstrual cycles
Can be removed if you want to conceive

❌ Cons
Must be inserted and removed correctly
Doesn’t protect against STIs
May cause nausea or vaginal irritation


* Available at Zapmed

4. Condoms (Male & Female) 

Best for: Anyone looking for dual protection (pregnancy and STIs).

What is it?

Condoms act as a physical barrier, preventing sperm from reaching the egg while also offering STI protection.

Pros & Cons

✅ Pros
Protects against STIs and pregnancy
No hormones = no side effects
Affordable and widely available

❌ Cons
Can break or slip if not used correctly
Some people have latex allergies (latex-free options exist)

5. The Implant 🪡

Best for: People who want long-term birth control with no daily reminders.

What is it?

A small, flexible rod inserted under the skin of the arm, slowly releasing progestin for up to three to five years.

Pros & Cons

✅ Pros
Long-term protection (three to five years)
Over 99% effective

❌ Cons
Can cause irregular bleeding at first
Requires a minor procedure for insertion/removal

6. The Injection 💉

Best for: People who don’t want to take a pill daily.

What is it?

The contraceptive injection is a progestin-only shot given every two to three months that prevents ovulation.

Pros & Cons

✅ Pros
Low-maintenance (one injection protects you for months)
